name: Example – discharge home (escape room)
description: Take Glenda's notes to the doctor, get her discharge letter, get through the key safe, then find out why her legs are swelling.

items.name: Glenda's notes
pages:
Ward 4 · Glenda Morris, 74
Heart failure, AF, type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure.
Admitted with breathlessness and swollen legs.

Medicines going home
Furosemide 40 mg every morning (water tablet)
Bisoprolol 2.5 mg · Ramipril 5 mg · Metformin 500 mg twice a day · Aspirin 75 mg

Plan
District nurses to visit within 48 hours: legs, weight, medicines.
Take these notes to Dr Shah for the discharge letter.

items.name: Discharge letter
pages:
Discharge letter: Glenda Morris (74)
Going home to live alone, with district nurse visits.
Key safe by the front door: code 1952.

items.name: Furosemide 40 mg
items.description: Her water tablets. The box hasn't been opened, and the label is dated three weeks ago.

rooms.name: Ward 4
rooms.intro:
Glenda (74) is going home today.
Find her notes in the bed bay and take them to Dr Shah for her discharge letter.

markers.label: Notice board
markers.title: Ward 4 – discharge day
markers.text: Patients going home today need: a discharge letter, their medicines explained, and a plan for community follow-up.

markers.label: Dr Shah
markers.text: Dr Shah: Have you got Glenda's notes? I can't write her letter without them.

accepts.feedback: Dr Shah: Thank you. Here's her discharge letter. The key safe code is on it.

markers.wrongText: Dr Shah: That's not what I need. I need her notes.

markers.label: To Glenda's home
markers.lockedText: You need Glenda's discharge letter first. Dr Shah writes it.
markers.codePrompt: Glenda's key safe. Enter the code from her discharge letter.

markers.label: Before she goes
markers.text: Which check matters most before Glenda goes home?

options.text: Her medicines and how she will take them
options.feedback: Yes. Look out for her medicines when you visit.

options.text: That her TV licence is paid
What she would like for lunch
options.feedback: Food matters, but think about safety first.

rooms.name: Glenda's living room
rooms.intro: You let yourselves in with the key safe. Look around before you start your assessment.

options.feedback: She tells you her legs are 'leaking'.

options.text: Check the kitchen and her medicines

markers.label: Furosemide box
markers.text: At the back of the worktop, behind the kettle, with a pile of other boxes.

markers.label: Glenda
markers.text: Glenda: Hello, dears. My legs are leaking again.

accepts.feedback:
Glenda: Oh, those. They make me run to the loo, so I stopped taking them.
That explains her swollen legs: talk to her about her medicines.
Glenda: I've read it, dear. What I want to know is why my legs are so bad.

markers.wrongText: Glenda isn't sure what you mean.

rooms.name: Glenda's kitchen
rooms.endText: Well done. Now agree the referrals Glenda needs before you leave.
